subject: AtlasSoft co-sell boundary sweep — account stitching & escalation path
messages:
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@atlassoft.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood + AtlasSoft account overlap — quick sync?

Hi Olga / Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our product team is excited about the connector. A quick heads-up: during our scoping call we surfaced ~18 mutual accounts where both AtlasSoft and Redwood are active. Our partnership team would like to propose a first-pass account mapping so we can avoid co-sell confusion and speed up joint pursuits.

Can you share how you typically handle:
- Account handbacks for deals already in progress
- A primary contact for escalation if an SDR/AE overlap happens mid-cycle
- A minimal mutual action plan (MAP) for opportunity qualification and responsibilities (sales + technical)

I'm attaching our account list export (Atlas_Account_Map_v2.xlsx) — it has account tiers and internal owners. Would be great to get a short playbook and an initial stitch suggestion by end of next week.

Cheers,
Megan
Partnerships Lead, AtlasSoft
[attachment: Atlas_Account_Map_v2.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@atlassoft.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood + AtlasSoft account overlap — quick sync?

Megan — thanks for the spreadsheet and context. I pulled this into our partner mapping template and did an initial sweep.

High-level notes:
- ~12 accounts are clear co-sell candidates (Atlas has platform integration interest + Redwood fits their stack).
- 6 accounts show potential conflict where an active AE is already running a deal we should avoid disrupting.
- 4 are low-touch/evangelism where we should default to Atlas as the primary channel.

Immediate proposals (short answer):
1) For active Redwood-led opportunities: we propose a soft handback policy — Atlas stays informed (weekly digest) and can join technical calls; Redwood retains primary AE and deal cadence unless Atlas brings a named exec sponsor.
2) For active Atlas-led opportunities where Atlas has procurement momentum: offer a quick-stitch where Redwood becomes the recommended integration vendor and we provide a joint quote to speed procurement.
3) For disputed accounts: kick to a 3-way review (Atlas partner lead + Redwood AE + our partnerships manager) and use a simple rubric: commercial momentum, technical fit, and existing PO/commitments.

I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (RDW-Atlas_MutualActionPlan.docx) — this is intentionally minimal: qualification checklist, split of discovery/technical due diligence, and procurement owner. Can you confirm whether Atlas can accept the procurement owner stay on the side with momentum?

Next steps:
- If that sounds reasonable, can we do a 30-min alignment on Thurs 2/18?
- After alignment, we’ll produce a per-account stitching file and propose owner flags (RDW-primary, ATLAS-primary, Dispute).

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Alliances Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: RDW-Atlas_MutualActionPlan.docx (docx)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: AtlasSoft boundary / escalation path (notes before call)

Olga / Marissa — quick internal notes for the call at 11:00 PT with Megan. Pulling together talking points and risk thresholds so we have a consistent stance.

Key risk thresholds (suggested):
- Commercial momentum threshold: if a deal has an executed PO or signed intent (LOI), we concede primary ops to the side with the PO and shift to joint close support.
- Technical momentum threshold: if Atlas has completed a production POC and is already providing pre-sales custom work, prefer Atlas primary unless Redwood has a named exec sponsor.
- Strategic stratification: for strategic >$500k ARR accounts, escalate to VP-level alignment before handing over ownership.

Escalation path (proposed):
1) AE-level attempt to stitch (within 2 business days)
2) Partner manager mediation (Olga / Megan) within 3 business days
3) If unresolved, escalates to Partnerships Director (Marissa / Atlas counterpart) for final decision within 5 business days

I'll bring the proposed per-account flags and the shortlist of disputed accounts. Also confirm: I want to keep our default approach to be "minimize churn for the customer" — i.e., avoid reassigning an active AE unless commercial momentum indicates we must.

Jonas
Sr. Director, Strategic Alliances (internal note)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@atlassoft.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood + AtlasSoft account overlap — alignment notes & next steps

Megan — great call this morning, appreciate the clarity. Following up with the concrete items we agreed on and owners.

Summary / Action Items (owners / due dates):
- Redwood will flag per-account ownership in the shared sheet and set initial flags (RDW-primary / ATLAS-primary / DISPUTE). Owner: Olga — due Mon 2/22 EOD.
- For accounts flagged DISPUTE, we will run a 3-way review using the rubric (commercial momentum, technical POC status, signed docs). Owner: Joint (Olga + Atlas Partner Lead) — review window Wed 2/24.
- Establish escalation timeline: AE-level stitch attempt (2 business days), partner manager mediation (3 business days), VP escalation for strategic deals >$500k within 5 business days. Owner: Jonas / Marissa (document escalation SOP).
- Mutual Action Plan adoption: Atlas to confirm acceptance of procurement owner rule (Atlas retains procurement momentum if they have active PO). Owner: Megan — please confirm by Tue 2/23.

Attachments: I uploaded the annotated account map and the agreed MAP to the shared Drive (link above).

If Megan confirms procurement rule, we’ll proceed to finalize flags and ship a trimmed partner-facing one-page playbook for AEs that shows the expected behavior when overlaps arise.

Thanks again — looking forward to a clean stitch.
Olga Petrov
Senior Alliances Manager, Redwood Inference
[link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bAtlasSoftMapping]
